Job Description
Aviation Electrician's Mate Organizational Level Technicians communicate with Maintenance Control and Quality Assurance work centers and operate

matches: Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.
Aviation Electrician's Mates (AE) maintain electrical and instrument systems, including power generation, conversion and distribution systems, aircraft batteries, and interior and exterior lighting.
Repair and maintain electrical and electronic controls for propulsion and braking systems.

and maintain electrical control of aircraft systems, including hydraulic, landing gear, flight control, utility, and power plant engine, flight and non-instrument-type indicating and warning systems, automatic flight control and stabilization systems, aircraft compass systems, attitude reference systems, inertial navigation systems, and environmental control systems.
Coordinate communications between air traffic control and maintenance personnel.

Aviation Electrician's Mate Organizational Level Technicians communicate with Maintenance Control and Quality Assurance work centers and operate according to the Naval Aviation Maintenance Program (NAMP).
Troubleshoot equipment, electrical components, hydraulics, or other mechanical systems.

maintain, troubleshoot, repair, and inspect a wide array of electrical and electronic equipment including: aircraft electrical systems, aircraft instrumentation equipment, aircraft power plant- and airframe-related equipment, and aircraft lighting equipment.
Troubleshoot robotic systems, using knowledge of microprocessors, programmable controllers, electronics, circuit analysis, mechanics, sensor or feedback systems, hydraulics, or pneumatics.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
